heading: Read this one twice
lede: The five slides before this describe a unit of account inside a set of local HTML files. This slide describes everything it isn't, and none of it is hedging — each line is a fact about the code.

flags.text: No chain, no contract, no deployment, no address that holds anything. 0x48455a45 is the ASCII for “HEZE” printed on a docket, not a function selector on any network.

flags.strong: Nothing here can be bought or sold.
flags.text: These files have no transfer, no order book, no custody and no counterparty. There is nothing to acquire, so nothing on these slides is an offer, a solicitation or a sale.

flags.strong: The dollar figures are a costing, not a valuation.
flags.text: $20,387,410 is what ten drawn hulls would cost to build at rates you can edit. Dividing it by 21,000,000 gives a ratio between two numbers in this project. It is not a price, it does not imply one, and no one is obliged to honour it.

flags.strong: Nothing is signed and nothing is sent.
flags.text: The address field is read locally to seed a drawing. There is no network call, no wallet connection, no signature request, and no key ever touches these files.
Nothing here is a recommendation to buy, sell or hold anything, and nobody involved is a licensed adviser.

closing: What it is: a design document for the unit a fictional shipyard quotes in, sitting alongside two files that draw ships and count their fastenings. That is the whole of it, and it is enough.
text: The disclaimer slide, stated at length on purpose: no token, nothing for sale, no valuation, no signing, no advice.
